page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-16 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 60 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 3.75 GB per core. It operates on the x86_64 architecture with dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring consistent performance without resource sharing.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). These hardware accelerators contribute to notable benchmark results, particularly in single-threaded tasks. The instance achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core testing and text processing, alongside strong results in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance, software compilation, and cryptography benchmarks fall within the average range.

This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled public IPv4 addresses, meaning storage must be provisioned externally. Memory bandwidth reaches 1380.8 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 109.68 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Given its high single-core efficiency and AMX-driven matrix math capabilities, the c4-standard-16 is well-suited for compute-intensive workloads, web serving, text processing, and lightweight machine learning inference, such as running small language models.
